newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares slide again on blue-chip sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares slide again on blue-chip sell-off.

text.p: The Nigerian stock market finished lower again in Thursday's trade, weighed down by continued selling of blue chip shares, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 8462.08 against 8470.33 on Wednesday.
Dealers said turnover was slightly above levels recorded earlier this week but added that investors' reluctance to hold their shares forced prices down.
They blamed the trend on Nigeria's economic distress, which has been worsened recently by fuel scarcity.
Petroleum marketers were among Thursday's main losers.
Agip fell 20 kobo to 18.00 naira while African Petroleum and Unipetrol were 10 kobo down at 55.90 naira and 67.90 respectively.
Leading insurer AIICO fell by 40 kobo to 14.40 naira.
Cadbury shed five kobo to end at 35.90 naira while Coca-Cola bottler Nigerian Bottling Company slid to 54.30 naira, down 10 kobo.
The brewing sector ended mixed. While Nigerian Breweries lost 10 kobo at 18.60 naira Guinness rose five kobo to 6.85 naira.
First Bank was two kobo weaker at 13.28 naira, Union Bank was five kobo down at 11.00 naira but FSB International Bank strengthened on its recent good results. It closed five kobo up at 4.55 naira.
Computer company NCR went ex-dividend on Thursday, down 33 kobo at 12.97 naira.
Investors remained uninterested in cement stocks as West African Portland Cement Company dropped 10 kobo at 62.30 naira and Ashaka Cement was down three kobo at 12.95 naira.
Hotly sought after food giant Nestle was steady at 50.00 naira.
